correctness.rationale: The classification into zero, two, and four transitions is exhaustive. The three two-transition families contain the complete middle run; only the two families beginning in zero can overlap, precisely at equal b,d and radii at most min(a,c,e). The four-transition family exists exactly when b=d and adds min(a,e) strings. Pairing the larger external zero run with c through max+min gives the displayed formula, with duplicate subtraction and the new four-transition family canceling the residual loss at b=d. If defect is k>0, both outer runs have length at least c+k and the unequal positive one-run lengths sum to at least three. Thus n>=2k+6. The tuple (k+1,1,1,2,n-k-5) attains each positive admissible k, and equal one-run lengths attain zero for every n>=5. The length-eight word 00101100 has defect one. The checker and verification note were read, not executed; a separate replay /workspace/branches/replay_frozen.py computed defects through longest palindromic suffixes for all 42504 positive five-part compositions at n=5–24 and confirmed the formula and the lengthwise spectra. The proof, not the finite replay, covers the unbounded claim.
